findings.finding: New treatment and medication paragraphs expressed treatment actions but were initially labelled explanation.
findings.resolution: Author relabelled p002-treatment-1 and p002-medications-1 as action. Retained placental management has CMA/NICE; component selection and medicine roles have CMA/NATA.

findings.finding: NICE-only recommendation against routine IV uterotonics solely for retained placenta lacked independent support for that exact prescribing restriction.
findings.resolution: Author removed that clause; retained causal management and TXA-versus-component explanation supported by CMA/NATA. Targeted final text reread in both languages.

resolution: Accepted as an editorial content candidate after targeted revisions, not clinician sign-off and not blanket ICD completion. Six changed sections read in Chinese and English; shared action conditions match. Existing blood-loss thresholds are attributed and not home waiting targets; new third-stage advice explicitly prohibits waiting for a minute threshold. No new dose, transfusion ratio or fixed follow-up schedule. All fourteen records and source hashes checked, including eight unchanged records.

category_decisions.rationale: Third-stage interval explicitly tied to vaginal birth; four causes remain possible. Added immediate action before placenta delivery, professional removal/analgesia and placental-versus-clotting pathways close the prior third-stage gap. General red flags, nutrition, daily care, psychological recovery, anaemia follow-up and next-pregnancy preparation apply after the acute event; this timing-defined leaf does not require a duplicate aftercare article.
category_decisions.exclusions_considered: Not all JA43 siblings; not retained placenta alone; do not assign caesarean-only haemorrhage to vaginal third-stage category; abnormal adherence decisions remain professional and conditional.

category_decisions.rationale: The draft correctly includes pre-existing and acquired clotting defects and does not reduce the leaf to DIC. Acute laboratory assessment and targeted components are adequately explained. However, inherited aftercare focuses on anaemia and future pregnancy without explicitly allocating postpartum haematology planning for a persistent/pre-existing clotting disorder. NATA recommendation10 calls for specific multidisciplinary care complementary to standard PPH management; source presence alone does not put this education in the article.
category_decisions.exclusions_considered: Covers relevant vaginal and caesarean PPH with clotting defects; not only DIC, not every isolated coagulation disorder without PPH, not every JA43 sibling.
remaining: Add a short bilingual, independently supported conditional follow-up branch for known or persistent clotting disorder and individual specialist plan; no need for exhaustive rare-disease dosing or a fabricated universal test interval.
